This common order shall govern disposal of miscellaneous appeal filed by the insurance company as well as cross objection (IA No.8411/2022) filed by the claimants as both the appeal as well as cross Reliance General Insurance Company ... vs Rahul on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157960633/
1 objection are arising out the same award.
2.

This appeal by the insurance company under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 13.09.2022 passed by 7th MACT, Ratlam in Claim Case No.11/2021 seeking reduction in the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
3. The cross objection (IA No.8411/2022) has been filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
By the impugned award the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.22,97,533/- along with interest for the permanent disability suffered by the claimant Rahul.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant/insurance company submits that the award passed by the Tribunal is on the higher side which deserves to be reduced and the cross objection filed by the claimant be dismissed.
5. On the other hand, counsel for the respondent/claimant has argued that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side which deserves to be enhanced by allowing the cross objection.

6. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the arguments advanced by the counsel for the parties and the evidence that came on record, I find no substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant.
The claimant/injured has suffered grievous injuries in the accident.
He sustained fracture in left leg as well as left hand.
It is a case of amputation of right leg of the injured from thigh.
The Tribunal has calculated 90% permanent disability and awarded the compensation in favour of the claimant.
Considering the gravity of the injuries sustained by the injured, the prolonged treatment and the loss of income suffered by him, I do not find any reason to reduce the said award amount.
Accordingly, the appeal filed by the insurance company has no substance and the same is dismissed.
7. So far as cross objection filed by the claimant/injured is concerned, I have gone through the impugned award as well as the evidence that came on record.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and going through the award, I find that no sum has been awarded by the Tribunal under the head of artificial limb, loss of amenities of life as well as future medical expenses to the claimant, therefore, in the considered opinion of this court, it would be just and proper to award a lump sum amount of Rs.1,00,000/- as further enhancement under the aforesaid heads over and above the amount which has already been awarded by the Tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.

For the enhanced amount of Rs.1,00,000/-, the Court fee shall be paid by the claimant within a period of one month, if already not paid, and thereafter the amount shall be released by the Insurance Company on receiving the certificate.

In case the certificate has not been filed before the Insurance Company up to a period of three months, the claimant shall not be entitled to receive the interest on the enhanced amount of compensation.
